expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected or claimed. Concretely: every permitted action fails its preconditions. rollback_image and revert_config both require a prior image tag or configuration recorded in change history and evidence of a deploy/config change inside the window — all four change-history dispatches died with the same response-parse error [tr_7c7136d87842, tr_53f4cca39479, tr_f3ae6788e684, tr_06833e7a95d8], so no prior tag or config is known to exist and no change is named. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; the only observation that ran is zero spans for nginx-web-server across 04:42:35-05:12:41 [tr_3c7a09c7f07e], a window lying almost entirely before the 05:12:35 alert, and the same source rules out reading an empty trace window as either health or outage. The Prometheus results [tr_ecf722d4c88a] establish that this silence is equally consistent with a standing export gap — nginx-web-server emits no traces that become metrics at all. The Loki query that would discriminate process_freeze from network_partition, disk_fill and bad_config was rejected with HTTP 400 for a malformed pod matcher and never executed [tr_ae542892c038]. scale_service, reconnect_service, restore_store and free_storage are listed UNAVAILABLE and cannot be proposed regardless. The next step is investigative, not remedial: re-run the Loki query with a corrected pod label matcher, and query Tempo for nginx-web-server over an earlier window on 2026-10-02 to learn whether this service ever emits spans.
if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the corrected Loki query returns nginx error lines clustered at 05:12:35 naming a specific upstream, or if a Tempo query over an earlier same-day window shows nginx-web-server emitting spans normally — either would convert the empty window into onset evidence and localise a mechanism, at which point restart_service on the named service becomes defensible. It is also wrong if the change-log tool recovers and shows a deploy or config edit on one of the four services inside the window, which would make rollback_image or revert_config the right class. Note that abstention's correctness cannot itself be confirmed by a metric: there is no series that goes green to prove not acting was right, which is part of why acting here would be unverifiable too — with span metrics structurally absent for all four services [tr_ecf722d4c88a, tr_df4845357d16, tr_ff29c4182d6f, tr_0a142cfdc055], no permitted action's effect could be measured as an error ratio falling or a latency percentile returning.
risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible impact if a real fault is active and untreated at the front door; nginx-web-server is the seed and alerted service, so whatever fired at 05:12:35 keeps firing. That risk is accepted because the alternative is worse: a speculative restart of nginx-web-server would discard its caches and reset every in-flight connection on the only ingress path, and if the true fault is a network partition, a filled disk, or a bad config, the restart either does nothing or returns the service to the same broken state while destroying the process-state evidence (open sockets, file descriptors, memory) that the pending Loki query is meant to read. A rollback or config revert on a service whose change history was never successfully read could install an arbitrary, possibly older-and-worse, image or point a dependency address somewhere stale.
blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. For contrast, had an action been proposed: a restart or rollback of nginx-web-server would be seen by all external clients, as it is the seed and alerted front door, and by compose-post-service, home-timeline-service and user-timeline-service as dropped inbound connections during the recreate. An action on any one of those three candidate_cause services would be seen by nginx-web-server, which is their named inbound caller, and through it by external clients on the affected request paths.
